newsitem.title: UK: British nurses held in Saudi Arabia murder probe.
newsitem.headline: British nurses held in Saudi Arabia murder probe.

text.p: Two British women nurses have been detained in Saudi Arabia by police investigating the murder of an Australian nurse at a military hospital, the Foreign Office in London said on Monday.
The nurses have been held in a Dhahran prison since Friday and have so far been denied access to the British consul in Saudi Arabia, a spokesman said.
And according to a British newspaper report, up to 40 British employees at the King Fahd Military Medical Complex have been refused access to their passports and told they cannot leave Saudi Arabia.
The Foreign Office said the Australian nurse was murdered in a hospital in Dhahran on December 11.

"The Saudi police investigating it have been questioning other medical staff at the hospital. I can confirm that they have detained two British nationals for questioning. It is not clear that they have been arrested or charged.
"The consul has flown down from Riyadh to Dhahran and is trying to do as much as he can for other British medical staff in the hospital.
"He is seeking consular access to the two. He had not been able to see them yet, but will try again tomorrow," the spokesman said.
The Daily Telegraph newspaper named the dead nurse as Yvonne Gilford, 55. It said she was found dead in her room and had been stabbed four times, hit with a hammer and smothered.
The newspaper, quoting hospital sources, said security officials had imposed a blanket ban on all foreigners leaving the complex immediately after the murder.

After the arrest of the two British nurses, who have not been named, this was relaxed for all nationals except those from Britain, Australia and South Africa -- a total of about 100 employees, the Telegraph said.
